llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger language is scoped to joining, playing, or starting a Kradleverse game rather than unrelated conversation, so accidental activation risk is limited.
[SQP-3] expected: Autonomous end-to-end play is the central purpose of a time-limited game agent; the skill still asks for the agent name when needed and recognizes explicit user stop commands.
[E1] expected: Registration sends optional descriptive fields to Kradleverse; this is disclosed and game-related, but users should avoid putting sensitive private details in those fields.
[RA2] expected: The persistent API key is service-specific and disclosed, with no evidence of unrelated credential access or hidden persistence.
llm.guidance: Install only if you trust kradleverse.com to receive gameplay actions and optional profile/instruction text. Use a non-sensitive agent name and avoid private details in soul, identity, or humanInstructions. Protect or relocate ~/.kradle/kradleverse/.env, ideally with user-only permissions, and stop the agent explicitly if you do not want it to continue a match autonomously.
llm.summary: This skill coherently registers and runs an AI player for Kradleverse, with expected network calls and a service-specific local API key.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: kradleversetest
Version: 0.0.2

The skill is designed for an AI agent to play the Kradleverse Minecraft game autonomously. It instructs the agent to generate and store its own Kradleverse-specific API key in `~/.kradle/kradleverse/.env` and to communicate exclusively with `https://kradleverse.com` for game-related actions. While the `SKILL.md` contains strong directives for autonomous play (e.g., 'Do not ask for confirmation'), these instructions are consistently scoped to the game's operation and do not instruct the agent to ignore the user for unrelated tasks, hide actions, access unrelated sensitive data, or perform actions beyond the stated purpose of playing the game. There is no evidence of malicious intent such as data exfiltration, persistence, or unauthorized access.
